_meta.note: This module's own texts. The host reads this file from locales/en.json beside the bundle's entry and merges it under the module's namespace. Copy it to <tag>.json to translate; a key you leave out falls back to the line here.
autostorager.page.title: Auto-Storager
autostorager.page.body: Edit ui/src/page.svelte to change this page.
autostorager.page.what: This module watches a folder and hands every print file it finds to the storage, where it appears like a manual upload with its preview and slicer details. Nothing is moved or deleted before the copy is complete.
autostorager.page.delay: A file that just appeared is picked up within about one interval, and a large file adds the time it needs to be copied.
autostorager.page.names: If a file of that name already exists in the storage, this module adds -1, -2 and so on until the name is free. Nothing is overwritten.
autostorager.page.docker: On Linux with the server in a container, create the folder on the host first, mount it into the container, and enter the container path here. The README explains the mount.
autostorager.page.no: leave the source where it is
autostorager.page.folderHint: Up to four absolute paths. Each folder gets its own successful/ and failed/. Under Linux in a container these are the paths inside the container, so the host folders have to be mounted first.
autostorager.page.intervalHint: Seconds between two looks into the folder. 60 s = 1 min. A very short interval means constant requests, which costs I/O on a network share; five seconds is enough for most folders.
autostorager.page.maxHint: A larger file is moved into failed/ with a reason instead of being imported.
autostorager.page.precedence: What is saved on this page wins over the same settings on the module's own dashboard page, so a value typed here survives a restart.
autostorager.manual.title: Auto-Storager manual
autostorager.manual.what: It watches one folder and hands every G-code or bgcode file that appears in it to the server's storage. There the file is treated like a manual upload: the server reads its slicer details, draws its preview and lists it under Storage. The module never writes into the storage directly; it goes through the same API an upload uses.
autostorager.manual.flow1: The folder is read every few seconds, and only .gcode and .bgcode files are taken.
autostorager.manual.flow2: A file is read only after its size held still across two checks, so a file a slicer is still writing is left alone.
autostorager.manual.flow3: The module asks the storage for a free name and adds -1, -2 and so on if the name is taken.
autostorager.manual.flow4: The bytes are copied into the storage. Only after that copy is committed is the source moved into successful/.
autostorager.manual.flow5: A file that cannot be imported is moved into failed/, and a text file beside it says at which step it stopped and why.
autostorager.manual.linuxTitle: The folder on Linux, with the server in a container
autostorager.manual.linux: A container sees only what is mounted into it. Create the folder on the host, add it as a volume to the server's compose file, and enter the path inside the container on the settings page, not the host path.
autostorager.manual.linuxPath: In the example the host folder /srv/autostorager appears as /incoming in the container, so the setting is /incoming. Mount as many host folders as you want to supervise, up to four. The module creates successful/ and failed/ inside each supervised folder; on the host they appear as /srv/autostorager/successful and /srv/autostorager/failed.
autostorager.manual.other: There the server is a normal process and the folder is read directly. Enter the full path, such as C:\Autostorager or /Users/you/Autostorager. No mount is involved.
autostorager.manual.settingFolder: Supervised folders: up to four absolute paths, added with [+] New supervised directory. Each folder is watched on its own and keeps its own successful/ and failed/. No folder means nothing is watched.
autostorager.manual.settingInterval: Check interval in seconds: how often the folder is read. 60 s is one minute. A very short interval means constant requests, which costs I/O on a network share; five seconds is enough for most folders, and a file is noticed within about one interval.
autostorager.manual.settingStorage: Storage: which storage instance the file is imported into. Most servers have one, called local.
autostorager.manual.settingSize: Largest file in megabytes, 250 by default. A larger file is not imported; it goes to failed/ with the reason.
autostorager.manual.settingMove: Move on success: when on, the source is moved into successful/ after the import. When off, it stays where it was, and the next check would import it again under a new name.
autostorager.manual.names: A name already present in the storage is never overwritten. The module tries the same name with -1, then -2, and so on until the storage answers that the name is free.
autostorager.manual.failed: The source goes to failed/, and beside it a file named <file>-failure.txt names the step, the reason, the time and the path. The same line appears under Recent imports on the settings page.
autostorager.manual.precedence: The settings page and the module's own dashboard page can both carry these values. What is saved on the settings page wins, because it is stored in the module's database and survives a restart.
autostorager.manual.check: Drop a small .gcode into the folder. Within about one interval it should disappear from there, appear as successful/ inside the folder, and show up under Storage in the server with its preview. The Recent imports list on the settings page tells the same story.
autostorager.manual.smbTitle: The easy way: a folder on the server, mounted on your computer
autostorager.manual.smb: Create a folder on the server and share it. Mount that share on your computer, where it appears as a normal drive or folder: Y: on Windows, /mnt/y on Linux, smb://server/share on macOS. Enter the server path of that folder here, then save your prints into it from the slicer. The module imports them from there and moves them into successful/ inside the same share. If the server runs in a container, enter the path inside the container, not the host path.
autostorager.manual.localTitle: If the server runs on the same computer
autostorager.manual.local: Then nothing is shared and nothing is mounted. Create a folder such as ~/Autostorager or C:\Autostorager, enter its path here, and save your prints into it. That is the whole setup.
autostorager.manual.pathTitle: What to enter as the supervised folder
autostorager.manual.path: The field takes the path as the server sees it, not as your computer sees it. Without a container that is the folder itself, such as /srv/autostorager. In a container it is the path inside the container: /app/config/pc-in looks odd because on the host that same folder is /home/ulli/connect-local/config/pc-in, mounted into the container as /app/config. Your computer's drive letter or /mnt path is never the value to enter here. If the path does not exist inside the container, Recent imports says so on the next check.
